:::{.callout-note}
This is a [design fiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Design_fiction).
Nothing here actually exists!

The purpose of this document is to speculate about a possible future, to make an idea
more real, to enable meaningful conversations.
:::

Based on responses from more than 200 geospatial professionals, the
[2026 CARTO State of Spatial Analytics Report](https://go.carto.com/report-state-of-spatial-analytics-2026-carto)
found that:

> ... spatial analysis rarely happens in a single tool.
> Fewer than 20% of respondents rely on just one platform, while the
> majority use between 3 and 8 tools to get work done -
> and it’s worth noting that the true number may be higher as only a limited
> selection of tools were given as options.

<TODO: Citation>

Working in multiple disparate tools creates a huge
[cognitive load](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive_load)
burden on practitioners.
Remembering how they worked in one tool after several
[context switches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_multitasking)
is very difficult -- often information is lost, leading to workflows that are
not reproducible or repeatable.

_Trail_ addresses this problem by creating a unified "trail map" of your
journey across compatible tools (like Jupyter Notebooks, JupyterGIS, and
JupyterDataConnect).
It provides facilities for visualizing, curating, and exporting information
about your workflow trail that can help you reproduce, operationalize, and
publish about your work.


## Try it now!

You can try out _Trail_ today.
Install it with `pip` or `mamba` (or similar tools):

:::{.panel-tabset}
### pip

```bash
pip install geojupyter-trail
```

### mamba

```bash
mamba install geojupyter-trail
```
:::


### How to use _Trail_

#### Setup

Once you've installed, turn on tracking with:

```bash
gj-trail init
```

This will set up a project directory so that any work done within it using compatible
tools will be recorded in to a Trailfile.

You can tell that a project is set up with _Trail_ by the presence of a
`.trail` directory at the root (similar to how you can identify a Git repo by a
`.git` directory at the root).


#### Tracking

Once _Trail_ is set up, any _Trail_-compatible tool used from that directory
will record your actions by default into a _Trailfile_
(`.trail/provenance.yml`).

This file can be read and edited by hand, but we recommend using our tools for
that instead!


#### Visualization & curation

To visualize or curate your _Trail_ with our web UI:

```bash
gj-trail view
```

This will open up the _Trail_ viewer in your browser.

Your trail might look something like this (`{...}` are placeholders for data,
for example a file path or a GeoJSON data structure or a code block):

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    classDef invisibleSubgraph fill:transparent, stroke:transparent;

    init[Project init]

    jdc-search["Search<br/>{...}<br/>w/ JDC "]
    jdc-acquire["Acquire data<br/>{...}<br/>w/ JDC"]

    data-written["Data written<br/>to project folder"]

    jgis-init["JupyterGIS<br/>Project init"]
    jgis-load["JGIS layer<br/>{...}<br/>added"]
    jgis-linger["JGIS viewport<br/>linger<br/>{...}"]
    jgis-draw["JGIS<br/>shape drawn<br/>{...}"]
    notebook-exec["Notebook cell<br/>{...}<br/>executed"]
    notebook-exec2["Notebook cell<br/>{...}<br/>executed"]
    notebook-exec3["Notebook cell<br/>{...}<br/>executed"]
    notebook-exec4["Notebook cell<br/>{...}<br/>executed"]

    data-written2["Data written<br/>to project folder"]


    init ~~~ jdc

    subgraph jdc[" "]
        jdc-search --> jdc-acquire
    end

    jdc ~~~ data-written
    data-written ~~~ jgis

    subgraph jgis[" "]
        direction LR
        jgis-init --> jgis-load
        jgis-load --> jgis-linger
        jgis-linger --> jgis-draw
    end

    jgis ~~~ nb

    subgraph nb[" "]
        direction LR

        notebook-exec ~~~ notebook-exec2
        notebook-exec2 ~~~ notebook-exec3
        notebook-exec3 ~~~ notebook-exec4
    end

    nb ~~~ data-written2

    class jdc invisibleSubgraph;
    class jgis invisibleSubgraph;
    class nb invisibleSubgraph;
```

This UI not only allows visualization, but also curation.
If, for example, you take a "detour" during your work to explore a method you
decide not to continue with, you can remove that element of your trail by
selecting it with click-and-drag, and pressing the DELETE key.
This will "hide" that element, and you can see it by clicking "Show hidden elements".
You can permanently delete it by following the same process again, or by using
SHIFT+DELETE the first time.

Read our [quick start](https://example.com) for more info about how to get started!


## How _Trail_ works

_Trail_ is always watching :eyes: (just kidding, edit this out later -- we want to avoid
"tracking" / "spying" implications, and we haven't fully fleshed out the architecture
yet).

```{mermaid}
sequenceDiagram
  actor user as User

  participant jupyter-data-connect as Jupyter<br/>Data<br/>Connect
  participant notebook as Jupyter<br/>Notebook
  participant jupytergis as JupyterGIS
  participant system as System

  box GeoJupyter Trail
    participant trail-cli as Trail CLI
    participant trail-service as Trail Service
  end

  user->>trail-cli: Initialize project

  user->>jupyter-data-connect: Search for data
    jupyter-data-connect->>trail-service: Event: Search
  jupyter-data-connect->>user: Results

  user->>jupyter-data-connect: Download data
    jupyter-data-connect->>trail-service: Event: Data acquisition

  system->>trail-service: Event: Data written to project folder

  user->>jupytergis: New JGIS project
    jupytergis->>trail-service: Event: Project (...) created

  user->>jupytergis: Import downloaded data
    jupytergis->>trail-service: Event: Layer (...) added

  user->>jupytergis: Observe area of interest (AOI)
    jupytergis->>trail-service: Event: Viewport linger (...)

  user->>jupytergis: Draw AOI polygon
    jupytergis->>trail-service: Event: Polygon drawn (...)

  user->>jupytergis: Buffer polygon
    jupytergis->>trail-service: Event: Buffered layer (...)
    jupytergis->>trail-service: Event: Layer (...) added

  user->>notebook: Clean downloaded data
    notebook->>trail-service: Event: Code cell (...) executed

  user->>notebook: Join downloaded data with cloud data
    notebook->>trail-service: Event: Code cell (...) executed

  user->>notebook: Perform calculation on joined data
    notebook->>trail-service: Event: Code cell (...) executed

  user->>notebook: Visualize results
    notebook->>trail-service: Event: Code cell (...) executed

  user->>notebook: Write output
    notebook->>trail-service: Event: Code cell (...) executed

  system->>trail-service: Event: Data written to project folder

  user->>trail-cli: Visualize trail
  user->>trail-cli: Prune trail to remove "detours"
  user->>trail-cli: Print citations
  user->>trail-cli: Print methods
```


## Technical details

_Trail_ runs as a service that registers project folders and monitors them for changes.
As a consequence, moving a _Trail_ project folder requires a special command
`trail project move ...` to both move the folder and update the registry.

:::{note}
The first release of Trail will likely not run as a service and exclude filesystem monitoring.
This design decision should wait until we've explored the problem space more thoroughly.
:::

When you run the `trail` CLI command, it traverses up the directory tree
looking for a `.trail` folder so it knows what project to operate on, even if
you're in a deeply-nested subdirectory (similar to Git).

Events are recorded with a **push** model; all compatible applications know how
to speak to the _Trail_ service to record events.
_Trail_ does not actively monitor applications.

All events are recorded in a JSON file as a **disconnected**
[Directed Acyclic Graph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Directed_acyclic_graph).
Many operations, for example code execution, can't currently be linked to other
events they depended on, even if that dependency is real.
For example, `rasterio.open("my_geo.tif")` may logically be linked to an event
in which `my_geo.tif` was acquired with JupyterDataConnect, but the dependency
will not be represented as an edge in the DAG.
However, the order of these operations will be recorded via timestamp.

Visualization and curation of the _Trail_ provenance is done with a web
application for compatibility with all operating systems.
